title: Opening Up for a Look

patient.name: Mr Goh Wei Ming
patient.presenting_complaint: Doctor has ordered pupil dilation so the back of both eyes can be examined

history.hpc: Mr Goh says 'Doctor want to dilate my eyes to check the back, then I will be blur for a while is it?' Both eyes are to be dilated for a fundus examination. He drove himself to clinic today.
history.pmhx: No narrow-angle history. No drug allergies (confirm). Wears glasses for distance.
history.social_hx: Drove himself to the clinic — relevant to post-dilation advice.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Deep anterior chambers, no contraindication to dilation noted by the doctor
examination_findings.fundus: To be examined by the doctor after dilation

investigations.task: Dilate both eyes safely for the fundus examination, documenting pre-dilation pupil size, the drops and dosage used, and the time
investigations.key_points: Confirm identity, eyes to dilate and allergy; check there is no narrow-angle contraindication; record pre-dilation pupil size for each eye; instil tropicamide (and phenylephrine if charted); note the time; warn about blur and light sensitivity

diagnosis: Both eyes are dilated safely for the fundus examination. Identity, eyes to dilate, allergy and the absence of a narrow-angle contraindication are confirmed; pre-dilation pupil size, the drops/dosage and the time are documented; and the patient is warned about temporary blurred near vision and light sensitivity. This is a procedural station.

immediate: Confirm identity, the eyes to dilate (both) and the doctor's order
Check for drug allergy and confirm no narrow-angle contraindication
Record the pre-dilation pupil size in mm for each eye
Perform hand hygiene and instil the charted dilating drop(s) into the lower fornix (no-touch)
Note the dosage (number of instillations) and the time of instillation
Apply gentle nasolacrimal pressure and advise on the effects
Document the eyes, drops, dosage, pupil sizes and time
follow_up: Inform the doctor of the dilation time so the fundus exam is done when adequately dilated
Re-check dilation if the pupils are not yet wide enough
patient_education: Explain why the eyes are being dilated and that vision will be blurred for a few hours
Warn about light sensitivity and advise not to drive until it wears off
Advise returning if there is eye pain or marked discomfort after dilation

key_points: Confirms identity, the eyes to dilate and the order
Confirms no narrow-angle contraindication before dilating
Asks how the patient travelled (driving) for post-dilation advice
Records pre-dilation pupil size in mm for each eye
Instils the charted dilating drop with a no-touch technique
Notes the dosage and the time of instillation
Understands the purpose of dilation for fundus examination
Knows narrow angles are a contraindication to check first
Knows what to document (pupil size, drops, dosage, time)
Recognises adequate dilation is needed before the exam
Documents eyes, drops, dosage, pupil sizes and time
Informs the doctor of the dilation time
Warns about blur, light sensitivity and not driving
